song.album: Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness

guitar.guitaristsText: Billy Corgan; James Iha is credited as band guitarist, but his contribution to the studio guitar tracks is not documented
guitar.modelsText: Stratocaster-style guitar with Lace Sensor pickups is supported at album level; the exact guitar and pickup selection for 1979 are unconfirmed
guitar.evidence: Billy Corgan states that Mellon Collie electric guitars were primarily Stratocasters with Lace Sensor pickups and his custom rack. Contemporary accounts identify Corgan and Flood as the principal creators of the final 1979 arrangement. No reliable song-specific source confirms a Reverend, Gibson Les Paul, exact pickup position, amplifier, pedal, microphone, or cabinet.
guitar.notes: Target is the 1995 studio album version. Billy Corgan is the safest principal-guitar attribution. Reverend guitars belong to later periods and are removed. Gibson models are not retained without song-specific evidence. The recording uses extensive looping, sampling and electronic processing. E-flat standard is a practical performance tuning, not a verified studio fact.
guitar.source: Guitar Player — Billy Corgan on 30 years of Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness: https://www.guitarplayer.com/music/billy-corgan-on-smashing-pumpkins-melon-collie-and-the-infinite-sadness ; Tape Op — Smashing Pumpkins: A Studio History: https://tapeop.com/interviews/115/smashing-pumpkins-a-studio-history ; Guitar World, January 1997 — King B's / 1979 notes: https://www.starla.org/articles/gw5.htm

tone.target: 1995 studio album version: compressed, warm Strat-style rhythm guitar integrated with sampled vocals, looped drums and electronic production
tone.profile: clean-to-edge-of-breakup electric rhythm with tight compression, rounded attack and subtle spatial movement
tone.summary: The identifiable character comes less from a documented chorus-and-delay pedal chain than from restrained guitar, compression, layering, loops and studio processing.
gearClues: Lace Sensor pickups at album level
Billy Corgan custom rack at album level
Marshall JCM 800 used extensively on the album
corrections: remove Reverend and Les Paul claims
replace prominent chorus with subtle modulation

rig.name: Smashing Pumpkins - 1979 Studio - Valeton GP-180
rig.recommendedGuitar: Strat-style guitar in E-flat standard; start with middle or neck-plus-middle pickup, moderate guitar volume and full tone control

blocks.purpose: Stabilize the palm-muted rhythm and approximate the controlled studio envelope.
blocks.gap: The original compression chain and settings are not documented.

blocks.purpose: Represent Corgan's documented album-era JCM 800 foundation at a clean-to-edge-of-breakup setting.
blocks.gap: The amplifier used specifically on 1979 has not been reliably identified.

alternatives.reason: Use when the UK 800 remains too grainy or compressed for the guitar and monitoring system.
Use for a softer British midrange and less aggressive preamp character.

blocks.purpose: Provide a restrained British cabinet response without excessive high-frequency bite.
blocks.gap: The song-specific cabinet, speakers and microphone placement are undocumented.

alternatives.reason: Pair with US Deluxe for a cleaner and more open adaptation.
Use for more upper-mid texture if the main model sounds too dark.

blocks.purpose: Keep the rhythm audible beside the loop while suppressing excessive bass and glassy treble.
blocks.gap: This is practical GP-180 mix shaping, not a historical setting.

alternatives.reason: Use when narrower frequency control better suits the guitar or playback system.

blocks.purpose: Approximate the slight movement and width created by layered studio processing.
blocks.gap: No reliable source confirms a chorus pedal on the studio guitar. The effect substitutes for unavailable layering and loop processing.

alternatives.reason: Use at very low depth when a softer cyclic movement blends better with the backing track.

blocks.purpose: Place the guitar inside the production without producing an obvious reverb tail.
blocks.gap: The original ambience is part of the complete studio mix rather than a documented guitar effect.

alternatives.reason: Use with a lower mix when a smoother ambience is needed.

improvements.summary: The main remaining gap is the sampled and layered production, not a missing conventional guitar pedal.

proposals.recommendedAsset: Backing track containing the drum loop, sampled vocal motif and electronic layers
proposals.reason: These elements provide much of the record's movement and cannot be recreated by the guitar preset alone.
proposals.whenToUse: For performance matching the 1995 studio version
proposals.expectedGain: Much closer rhythmic feel and overall identity

proposals.recommendedAsset: Moderately dark Marshall-style 4x12 IR with an off-axis dynamic microphone
proposals.reason: Refines the album-era British foundation without introducing harsh modern treble.
proposals.whenToUse: When the stock UK Vintage 4x12 sounds boxy or aggressive
proposals.expectedGain: Smoother attack and more convincing midrange

proposals.reason: Layered width is more appropriate than increasing the GP-180 chorus depth.
proposals.whenToUse: During recording or with stereo processing available
proposals.expectedGain: Wider sound with less obvious modulation
